developments.text: BLM's Red Desert Complex daily reports: 109 horses gathered on Oct 24 and 80 shipped, with no deaths. On Oct 23 BLM put down four horses (two of them blind, two with limb deformities), which it lists as pre-existing conditions. The daily reports add up to 776 gathered since Oct 16, against a fall target of about 1,035 from the Stewart Creek and Green Mountain areas.

Arizona, California and Nevada say they have sent the federal government a plan to save up to 3.2 million acre-feet of Colorado River water through 2028, adding at least 700,000 acre-feet of conservation to the 1.25 million acre-feet a year in cuts they proposed earlier. It still needs approval from the Arizona Legislature and California and Nevada water boards. The states say they are open to the Upper Basin's call for mediation.
developments.source_name: Lower Basin states' news release (reprinted by CRIT Manataba Messenger)

developments.text: Colorado River negotiators for the Upper and Lower basins appeared together but showed little sign of agreement. One idea discussed was three mediators: one picked by each basin and a third picked by those two. The Senate Energy and Natural Resources Committee has scheduled a hearing on post-2026 river rules (date not given in the article).

BLM signed an environmental assessment renewing 15 reindeer grazing permits for 10 years on about three million acres of the Seward and Baldwin peninsulas in Alaska, with room for up to five more permits. BLM ties it to the Reindeer Industry Act of 1937 and Alaska Native herding.
developments.source_name: BLM news release (reposted by World Online)

developments.text: The Cloud Foundation holds its 'Born to Be Wild' gala in Colorado Springs.

Mountain West News Bureau reports that Agriculture Secretary Brooke Rollins sent letters this month to governors of states with wolves, asking Arizona, New Mexico and Colorado to review and possibly drop state wolf protections and asking Idaho, Wyoming and Montana to keep their hunting policies. Food and Water Watch's Mitch Jones says it will not lower beef prices; an American Farm Bureau Federation analysis puts wolf costs to ranchers at $128 million a year.
BLM's Red Desert Complex page reports 666 horses gathered, 508 shipped and 11 deaths as of Oct 23. The plan is about 1,035 removals this fall. BLM labels the deaths pre-existing or chronic.
Return to Freedom posts that more than 650 horses have been captured and seven killed in south central Wyoming. Seven matches WHE's Oct 20 count; BLM's Oct 23 count is 11.
Skydog Ranch posts say a Times (UK) report found horses sold at a BLM event in Hugo, Oklahoma ('Bowie 41') mostly went to Mexico. I did not open the article.
Colorado Newsline opinion by Sammy Herdman on the proposed federal grazing rules and cattle ranchers. It is an opinion piece. PLC says BLM's proposed grazing rule (RIN 1004-AE82) is not final.

More than 55 groups, including Conservation Colorado, Trout Unlimited, TRCP, BHA and WRA, back Colorado Proposition 137, which they say would direct about $175 million a year to water, wildfire and open space without raising tax rates.
BLM concludes the North Complex gather in Washoe County, Nevada (first there since 2012): 323 horses gathered, 322 shipped. Estimate 424 against AML 101 to 157; target was about 320.
Santa Barbara News-Press feature on Return to Freedom, reposted by the group: about 400 horses and 50 burros in care, costs above $240,000 a month, push for the SAFE Act.

BLM began aerial herbicide treatment on about 23,600 acres at Jacks Creek, Idaho (Oct 23, up to three weeks) with Pheasants Forever and the U.S. Wildland Fire Service. BLM says wildfires burned over 3.3 million acres of BLM land this year.

CBD says only 3 species were listed under the Endangered Species Act in nearly two years, 39 FY2026 findings were missed, and a July workplan dropped 64 species. CBD's counts; not checked against FWS.

TRCP reports BLM is taking nominations for projects to open landlocked public land (Dingell Act lands, at least 640 contiguous acres, LWCF-funded). TRCP cites a 2018 count of 9.52 million landlocked acres in 13 western states. BLM's notice not opened.

Colorado BHA says a proposed GAME Act would swap about 2,158 acres of BLM land near Glenwood Springs for about 2,103 acres on the Roan Plateau. The bill has not been introduced and Colorado Parks and Wildlife does not endorse it.

BLM concludes the emergency Riddle Mountain gather in Oregon. BLM reports a 12-year-old mare euthanized for a fractured leg. Court order allowed up to 140 horses of a herd of about 418, leaving 278 on the range.
WyoFile reports a Path of the Pronghorn bottleneck near gas leasing is now protected by a 169-acre easement and a route designation.

BLM's acting Rock Springs district manager, Mike Gates, told the Rocket Miner the agency plans a new road around Red Creek Ranch south of Rock Springs after the landowner tore up the public access road. He expects environmental clearances over the winter and the project ready by next summer.
OPB reports BLM began capturing about 140 Riddle Mountain horses after the Bald Mountain Fire. BLM's Oct 19 release calls it an emergency rescue after a delay caused by a restraining order.

WHE says BLM's Karen Budd-Falen announced rewrites of the Wild Horse and Burro rules, with a draft for public comment expected before year end. Also says $30M USDA plus $11M in the Interior budget will come with no guardrails.

PERC argues grizzly recovery is working and backs the proposed tiered 4(d) rule; says Yellowstone-area bears grew from 136 in 1975 to over 1,000. FWS's grizzly rulemaking page shows a comment period through Aug 17 and no final rule.

BLM begins a bait-trap gather on the Pryor Mountain Wild Horse Range, Montana: about 100 to be gathered, up to 37 removed, others treated with fertility control and released. BLM estimate is 187 horses against AML 107 to 120. (WHE says 185.)

KSFR reports on new threats to New Mexico's Mexican wolves from border wall construction and a possible delisting. EO 14425 (Sept 4; https://thefederalregister.org/documents/2026-18571/supporting-america-s-ranchers) directs Interior to decide whether gray and Mexican wolves meet delisting or downlisting criteria; its report is due about Dec 3.

CBD says it and Western Watersheds Project moved to intervene to defend sage-grouse protections against an oil industry lawsuit by Western Energy Alliance and Wyoming. CBD's account; court docket not opened.
CWP's new BLM Data Center Tracker lists at least 35 active data center applications covering over 24,000 acres in six Western states. Many list no acreage. CWP's own tracker.

Reclamation weekly update (as of Oct 18): Lake Powell 3,520.55 ft (23% full), Lake Mead 1,037.24 ft (26% full); total system storage 18,128 kaf (31%) versus 37% a year ago; WY2027 Powell unregulated inflow forecast 39% of normal. Kiowa County Press reports Mead record lows on Oct 9 and Oct 15 and Powell's low on Sept 15.
developments.source_name: Bureau of Reclamation; Kiowa County Press

developments.text: BLM concludes the Sulphur gather in western Utah (about 300 planned; AML 165 to 250). Daily totals are on the BLM page; I did not total them. A search summary gave 259 gathered and 2 deaths.

A federal judge reopened the lawsuits over the cuts to Bears Ears and Grand Staircase-Escalante monuments. Requires 48 hours' notice before ground-disturbing activity on lands cut out of the monuments.
A federal judge (D. Or., Karin Immergut) grants a preliminary injunction against the full Riddle Mountain roundup, in a suit by OWHO, COWHC and Western Watersheds Project.
BLM announces the Red Desert Complex gather in Wyoming: about 1,035 horses this fall (about 1,800 over time). Estimate 2,278 against AML 480 to 720. Horses go to Wheatland.
Ninth Circuit heard appeals on gray wolf protections (three appeals from 14 challenges). Defenders of Wildlife's attorney argued against removing protections. No ruling reported yet.

USGS Data Report 1234 updates the greater sage-grouse range-wide trend: 2.7 percent average annual decline 1966-2021, cumulative declines of 42.4, 61.7 and 77.9 percent over the periods it reports, and a 1.9 percent decline 2024-2025. Missing Wyoming data biases the estimates.
Western Energy Alliance President Melissa Simpson backs the Senate permitting bill (S. 5653) as balancing energy and the environment.
CWP analysis: 99.1 percent of the 370,238 comments posted on the Roadless Rule rescission oppose it. The proposed rule was published Aug 20. CWP's own count of posted comments.

Forest Service comment period on rescinding the Roadless Rule closed after a 15-day extension. BHA says it sent 98,981 messages; about 58.2 million acres are inventoried roadless and the rescission would remove 44.7 million acres, 9.3 million in the Tongass. GYC says supporters sent 31,561 comments in 45 days (GYC blog: https://greateryellowstone.org/blog/2026/gyc-supporters-send-30000-comments-to-usda-in-support-of-the-roadless-rule). Acreage figures differ by source (44.7, 58.2 and 58.5 million).
Ninth Circuit appeal 26-6528 docketed in the American Prairie grazing permit case. Opening brief due Nov 2; answering brief due Nov 30.
WHE says the Congressional Wild Horse Caucus has asked GAO to audit the BLM sale program, and that the Pancake Complex case (NV) is in final briefing.

S. 5653, the 'Bipartisan American Affordability and Jobs Act of 2026', was introduced by Sens. Capito, Lee, Whitehouse and Heinrich and sent to the Senate Energy and Natural Resources Committee. The Wilderness Society lists six public lands concerns; WEA backs it.
TRCP named Jessica Turner president and CEO, starting Nov 9, 2026. Matt Cook is interim CEO until then.
Sand Wash Basin gather (Colorado) concludes: about 245 removed, 55 released (22 mares treated with fertility control), no deaths. Estimate 505 against AML 163 to 362.
AWI calls BLM's $30M fertility-control plan welcome but vague. It notes 921 treatments in FY2025 versus about 14,000 equines targeted for removal in FY2026.
BLM announces a $30 million USDA investment to expand fertility control, and a national roundtable. Details such as vaccine type and herds were not given.
BHA's September roundup lists H.R. 10529, Rep. Zinke's 'A River Runs Through It Act' (about 430,000 acres in Montana), introduced Sept 21. Bill text not opened; this is BHA's summary.
Public Lands Council held its 58th annual meeting Sept 15-17 at Copper Mountain, CO. President Tim Canterbury and others described policy wins and challenges for public lands ranchers.

President signed EO 14429, 'Reinvigorating America's Hunting Heritage'. Within 90 days: allow hunting in Castle Mountains and Craters of the Moon national monuments. Within 180 days: policies to expand access, including permitting lead ammunition. TRCP welcomed it on Sept 18.

CBD says an FWS directive from Director Brian Nesvik dated Sept 14 narrows the Endangered Species Act definition of 'take' and would allow killing of endangered wildlife. CBD's account; I did not open the directive.

BLM's project page for the Rock Springs Special Management RMP Amendment (Red Desert) shows status 'In Progress - Analysis & Document Preparation', last updated Sept 16. No draft plan is posted. Planning area lists 12 ACECs, 5 SRMAs and 13 WSAs. BLM's 2025 release says about 1.3 million acres; WyoFile says 3.6 million. I could not reconcile this.
Judge Brian Morris (D. Mont.) grants a preliminary injunction for three American Prairie allotments (Telegraph Creek, Box Elder, Whiterock) after BLM revoked six bison grazing permits on May 8.

NYT (Dave Philipps; Seattle Times copy): BLM sales more than doubled to about 3,700 in 2025. One Ohio buyer got about 500 horses at $25 each. BLM did not answer questions and says it does not sell to slaughter. Skydog's Clare Staples is quoted.
Salt River Wild Horse Management Group says Gov. Hobbs suspended removals and adoptions of Salt River horses until 2028, raising the herd target from 120 to 170.
developments.source_name: Salt River Wild Horse Management Group

developments.text: Return to Freedom welcomes BLM's new sale terms: the bill of sale bars 'recklessly or negligently' selling for slaughter. BLM's sales page now shows fees starting at $125 per animal (it was $25).
developments.source_name: Return to Freedom; BLM sales page

developments.text: American Prairie sues in D. Mont. (4:26-cv-00282) over the permit revocations.

Judge William Shubb (E.D. Cal.) granted a preliminary injunction on Jul 7 blocking BLM gathers at Carter Reservoir, Buckhorn and Coppersmith (470, 273, 113 horses). WHE says BLM is appealing to the Ninth Circuit.
BLM revokes six American Prairie bison grazing permits. Older than 90 days; included as context.
WyoFile: BLM delays Wyoming checkerboard removals (Rock Springs) to about October 2026 after the Tenth Circuit's Jul 15, 2025 ruling (No. 24-8055). Older than 90 days.
WHE says BLM's 2026 population report is 'a political tool': it counts 70,092 as excess using the low AML total of 15,374. Older than 90 days.

Not opened, so left out of developments: Roll Call report that the House FY2027 Interior bill (H.R. 9171) has $144M for the program; the SAFE Act status; Idaho Challis gather (226 horses).
The Salt River horses are managed by Arizona and the Forest Service, not BLM.

This file broadens the horse rescue tracker to western conservation, hunting and angling, ranching and industry voices. Public Lands Council (plc), American Prairie (american-prairie), Western Watersheds Project (wwp) and BLM (blm-whb) are already in data.json and are linked by id in 'related'.

Western Values Project is not listed. Its site (westernvaluesproject.org) now serves casino spam. InfluenceWatch (modified 2026-05-01) and a political email archive say it is integrating with Accountable.US. Status not confirmed.

Acreage differences, unresolved: Rock Springs plan area is about 1.3 million acres in BLM's Oct 2025 release and 3.6 million in WyoFile. Roadless acres appear as 44.7 million (rescission), 58.2 million (BHA) and 58.5 million (PERC).

Citizens for the Red Desert's site looks dated (references 2021) and may be dormant. Wyoming Outdoor Council, Wyoming Wildlife Federation and Wyoming Wilderness Association X accounts have no posts since 2023.

Center for Biological Diversity's X profile says it no longer uses X. X follower counts and last post dates were read on 2026-10-24. No official X handle found for CWP, Conservation Colorado, Great Old Broads, WRA, WSGA or Citizens for the Red Desert.
Financials are the latest year ProPublica posts (FY2023, WSGA FY2024); data lags. CWP is a project of the Resources Legacy Fund and has no separate record.

WRA's Colorado River Final EIS statement is dated July 31, 2026 (out of window). A search summary that said October was wrong. EO 14425 (Sept 4) and the Las Vegas land sale (BLM, Sept 10) are before the window and appear only as context.

Not confirmed, because I only saw them in search results: Montana's wolf quota cut to 300 (Daily Montanan, Aug 21), S. 5604 and its committee referral, the Utah v. Burgum case, and TRCP's Oct 23 permitting bill article. TWS's date on its S. 5653 post is missing.
